Based on the text provided, the legal precedents mentioned are **Smith v. Maryland** and **Jones v. United States**. The text notes that *Smith v. Maryland* established the third-party doctrine, which was subsequently applied in *Jones v. United States* to uphold the principle that individuals do not have a reasonable expectation of privacy for information voluntarily shared with third parties. The similarity to the case at hand (implied by the context of the retrieval) is the application of this third-party doctrine regarding privacy expectations.

The largest country in the world is Russia.
